items.stem: A model reports 99% accuracy classifying rare-signal events where only 1% of events are signal. Why is this metric misleading?

options.text: A classifier that labels everything 'background' also scores 99%, so accuracy ignores the rare class
options.rationale: Correct: with severe imbalance, accuracy is dominated by the majority class and hides poor signal recall.

options.text: Accuracy cannot be computed for physics data
options.rationale: Accuracy is computable; it is simply the wrong summary here.
The issue is the metric choice, not the value.
High accuracy here reflects imbalance, not necessarily overfitting.

items.explanation: Correct: with severe imbalance, accuracy is dominated by the majority class and hides poor signal recall.

items.stem: Which TWO steps help prevent data leakage when training a model on physical measurements? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Fit scalers and preprocessing only on the training split, then apply to validation and test
options.rationale: Correct: fitting preprocessing on all data leaks test information.

options.text: Keep repeated measurements of the same object within a single split
options.rationale: Correct: splitting correlated repeats across sets leaks information.

options.text: Choose the test set to contain the easiest examples
options.rationale: That biases evaluation and does not prevent leakage.

options.text: Train until the training loss reaches zero
options.rationale: That encourages overfitting and is unrelated to leakage.

items.explanation: Correct: fitting preprocessing on all data leaks test information.

items.stem: Building a known conservation law into a model's loss function is beneficial mainly because it

options.text: constrains predictions to be physically consistent and can improve generalisation from limited data
options.rationale: Correct: physics-informed constraints reduce unphysical solutions and help generalisation.

options.text: guarantees the model will never make an error
options.rationale: Constraints reduce but do not eliminate error.

options.text: removes the need for any training data
options.rationale: Data is still required to learn the task.

options.text: makes the model train faster in every case
options.rationale: Added constraints can slow or complicate training.

items.explanation: Correct: physics-informed constraints reduce unphysical solutions and help generalisation.
